title: PRA Privileged Desktops: AWS IAM policy and cross-account role templates

prose.text: Privileged Desktops is a PRA feature whose AWS side is prepared with two CloudFormation templates from the zscaler/zpa-privileged-desktops repository. The user-facing feature is not described by a captured help page {{gap:desktop-feature}}; see [[zpa.pra]] for PRA itself.

prose.label: Step 2, the role.
prose.text: {{role-parameters}} {{role-name-fixed}} {{trust-policy}} {{policy-then-role}} Which principals to trust and how the role is registered are open {{gap:principal-and-registration}}.

checks.do: Before creating the stacks, which account and region the policy targets, since the policy name carries the region.
Whether the permissions requested match what the security team will accept: tag-scoped for network and instances, unscoped for describe, key pair and stack actions.
Whether the trust policy needs an external ID or other condition, which the template leaves empty.

repo-purpose.statement: The zscaler/zpa-privileged-desktops repository is described as the repo for the Privileged Desktop feature of Privileged Remote Access (PRA), holding CloudFormation templates that establish the trust relationship and IAM role.

quotes: Repo for the Privileged Desktop feature of Privileged Remote Access (PRA). Cloud Formation Templates to establish trust relationships and IAM role.

two-steps.statement: The repository has two CloudFormation templates: permissions_policy_step_1.yml creates a customer-managed IAM policy and create_iam_role_and_trust_step_2.yml creates a cross-account role with a trust policy.

quotes: This template creates a customer-managed IAM policy for ZPA Privileged Remote Access (PRA)
This template creates the DJB-Cross-Account-Role with a trust policy

policy-purpose.statement: The step 1 policy is described as a customer-managed IAM policy for ZPA Privileged Remote Access (PRA) that grants the necessary permissions for creating and managing disposable jump boxes and other resources.

quotes: This template creates a customer-managed IAM policy for ZPA Privileged Remote Access (PRA) to grant the necessary permissions for creating and managing disposable jump boxes and other resources.

policy-parameters.statement: The step 1 template takes TargetAccountId (the AWS account where resources will be managed) and TargetRegion (the AWS Region) as parameters, and names the policy ZPA-PRA-Cross-Account-Policy-<TargetRegion>, so the policy is region-specific; it outputs PolicyArn.

quotes: The AWS Account ID where the resources will be managed.
The AWS Region where the resources will be managed.
The ARN of the created IAM policy.

role-parameters.statement: The step 2 template takes TrustedPrincipals, a comma-separated list of AWS principal ARNs allowed to assume the role, and ManagedPolicyArnsList, a comma-separated list of managed policy ARNs to attach, and outputs RoleArn and RoleId.

quotes: A comma-separated list of AWS principal ARNs that are allowed to assume this role.
A comma-separated list of managed policy ARNs to attach to the role.
The ARN of the created DJB-Cross-Account-Role.
The stable and unique ID of the created role.

role-name-fixed.statement: The role is named DJB-Cross-Account-Role in the step 2 template, and the step 1 policy grants iam:GetRole and iam:ListAttachedRolePolicies on the role of that name in the target account.

trust-policy.statement: The role's trust policy allows the TrustedPrincipals to call sts:AssumeRole with an empty Condition ({}), so the template adds no further condition such as an external ID.

network-scope.statement: The step 1 policy lets PRA create a VPC, subnets, route tables, an internet gateway and security groups only when the Name tag in the request matches *ZPA-PRA*, and delete a VPC or an internet gateway only when its Name tag matches *ZPA-PRA*.

instance-scope.statement: The step 1 policy allows ec2:RunInstances for instances only with a Name tag that starts with ZPA-PRA, and allows ec2:ModifyInstanceAttribute and ec2:TerminateInstances only on instances whose Name tag starts with ZPA-PRA.

untagged-scope.statement: The step 1 policy grants a set of EC2 describe actions plus ec2:CreateTags, ec2:CreateKeyPair and cloudformation:DescribeStacks on Resource "*", and cloudformation:CreateStack, cloudformation:DeleteStack and cloudformation:DescribeStackEvents on any stack in the target account and region.

policy-then-role.statement: The step 1 PolicyArn output is the managed policy to supply to the step 2 ManagedPolicyArnsList parameter.

quotes: The ARN of the created IAM policy.
A comma-separated list of managed policy ARNs to attach to the role.

policy-then-role.conditions: Assumes the ZPA-PRA-Cross-Account-Policy created by step 1 is the managed policy intended for the role; the repository README does not state the wiring.

principal-and-registration.title: Which principal to trust and how PRA is told about the role
principal-and-registration.detail: The repository does not say which AWS principal ARNs a customer should list in TrustedPrincipals, whether an external ID is expected, or where the resulting RoleArn is entered in the ZPA Admin Portal or API.
principal-and-registration.blocks: setting up a Privileged Desktops AWS account

desktop-feature.title: What Privileged Desktops provisions and its limits
desktop-feature.detail: No captured Zscaler help page describes the Privileged Desktops feature. The templates show the AWS resources PRA may create (VPC, subnets, internet gateway, security groups, instances, CloudFormation stacks), but the user-facing behavior, licensing, supported regions and session lifecycle are not documented in the repository.
